name: The New York Times
justification: The New York Times, the paper of record whose critics set the Broadway verdict; its London reviews are occasional and carry less market weight there. Keep the nyc1/lon2 split.

name: New York Stage Review
justification: New York Stage Review, founded 2018 by veteran critics from the major dailies (Frank Scheck, David Finkle, Steven Suskin and others), one of the highest-volume voices in the 2022+ corpus. Matches T2.

name: Variety
justification: Entertainment trade paper of record with staff critics; 612 NYC reviews and the largest share of the corpus. T1 in NYC; 13 London reviews where it is a secondary voice, keep T2.

name: Newsday
justification: Newsday's Linda Winer was one of the market-setting NYC critics for decades (366 reviews, highest normPct in this batch) until coverage ended in 2019; defunct for theatre reviews. Keep NYC T1 as it stood when publishing.

name: Theater Life
justification: Long-running NYC theatre review site with 516 reviews from 2007 to 2026 and one of the highest steady shares of the NYC corpus in both periods. A regular, aggregator-recognized voice; keep T2.

name: Scheckontheater
justification: Frank Scheck's personal review site; Scheck is a recognized critic (Hollywood Reporter, NYSR). Only 18 reviews in 2011 (inactive since); keep T3.

name: Talkin' Broadway
justification: Talkin' Broadway, a long-established theatre site with recognized regular critics and high sustained volume since 1997. Matches T2.

name: Backstage
justification: Backstage, the long-running trade publication for performers, which ran regular reviews until 2013 (93 reviews). Defunct as a review source; keeps the T2 tier that reflected its standing.

name: The Hollywood Reporter
justification: The Hollywood Reporter is a major entertainment trade whose chief theatre critic (David Rooney) is one of the market-setting NYC voices, with 403 NYC reviews. Its London coverage is minimal (4 reviews), so the existing NYC T1 / London T2 split stands.

name: Did They Like It
justification: Did They Like It (didtheylikeit.com) is a review aggregator, not an outlet. All 40 rows link to didtheylikeit.com, so they are aggregator pages filed under a fake outlet and should be reattributed to the original critics. Tier kept at current until then.

name: New York Daily News
justification: Major New York daily with long-serving staff critics (Joe Dziemianowicz and others), steady volume over decades. Matches T2.

name: Time Out New York
justification: Time Out New York has a highly regarded chief critic and a steady 498 NYC reviews, but it is a listings and culture magazine, and the rubric places Time Out at T2 alongside TheaterMania and NY Post, not with the NYT, Vulture, Variety tier. London tier unchanged (no London reviews). Considered NYC T1 to T2, not proposed: Time Out New York has a long-serving chief critic and is a leading NYC voice, so T1 stands.

name: The Wall Street Journal
justification: National daily with a long-serving staff drama critic; 450 NYC reviews. Market-setting on Broadway; keep.

name: The Washington Post
justification: Major national daily with a long-serving chief theatre critic; 330 NYC reviews. Keep T1 in NYC.

name: The Wrap
justification: Hollywood trade and entertainment news site with a long-serving theatre critic; 388 NYC reviews and sustained share. T2 fits.

name: DC Theatre Scene
justification: DC Theatre Scene, a Washington-area theatre site whose New York reviews came largely from Jonathan Mandell, with high volume 2015-2020. Kept at current tier.

name: Broadway News
justification: Broadway News (Broadway News, Inc.) is an active Broadway trade news site. Charles Isherwood reviewed for it from its 2017 launch until he became the Wall Street Journal critic in 2022; his 78 reviews here stay T1 either way because he is on the top-critics list. The other 136 reviews (mostly Brittani Samuel) are trade-site criticism comparable to TheaterMania, so propose NYC 1 to 2.

name: Vulture
justification: New York magazine's culture site with a leading staff theatre critic; 524 NYC reviews. Market-setting on Broadway; keep.

name: Deadline
justification: Deadline, a major entertainment trade publication with a staff Broadway critic, high sustained volume (318). Kept at nyc1/lon2.

name: New York Post
justification: Major New York daily with a staff theatre critic (Johnny Oleksinski), steady presence in both periods. Matches T2.

name: TheaterMania
justification: Major theatre-specialist site with staff critics, 513 NYC reviews and one of the largest shares of the corpus. Standard T2 per the rubric.

name: NBC New York
justification: NBC New York (Robert Kahn) reviewed Broadway regularly from 2013 to 2017 with 128 reviews and a high per-year share; its theatre coverage is now defunct. Keep T2 as it stood when publishing.

name: Front Row Center
justification: Front Row Center is a long-running NYC theatre review site with 368 reviews since 2013 and sustained per-year share (normPct 2.3). It is a regular critical voice, keep T2.

name: Theater Scene
justification: Long-running NYC theatre review site with a stable of experienced critics; 436 reviews and rising share since 2022. Regular aggregator-recognized voice; keep T2.

name: Entertainment Weekly
justification: Entertainment Weekly, a national entertainment magazine with sustained theatre coverage (435 reviews). Kept at T2.

name: amNewYork
justification: amNewYork, a free New York daily with a long-serving theatre critic (Matt Windman) and sustained volume (370 reviews since 2009). Fits T2 as an established local daily.

name: Chicago Tribune
justification: Chicago Tribune, whose long-serving critic Chris Jones is one of the most read US theatre critics, with sustained volume (311 reviews). Kept at T2.

name: Theatrely
justification: NYC theatre site founded 2021 with a team of contributors and an editor; 196 reviews and a high share of the 2022+ corpus. Regular aggregator-recognized voice; keep T2.

name: USA Today
justification: National daily with a long-serving theatre critic; 240 NYC reviews. Major daily fits T2.

name: NY1
justification: New York cable news channel whose theatre critic Roma Torre was a recognized Broadway reviewer and a strong regular presence in 2015-2019. Theatre reviews stopped in 2020 (defunct as a review source); keep the tier that reflected its standing.

name: The Guardian
justification: The Guardian is a major international paper; its London critics (Arifa Akbar and others) set the market and its US theatre coverage (Alexis Soloski and others) is a regular NYC voice with 252 NYC reviews. Keep T1 in both markets.

name: New York Theater
justification: New York Theater, Jonathan Mandell's long-running site; largely single-author but by a veteran journalist, picked up by aggregators and very consistent in volume since 2010. Keep T2.

name: The Komisar Scoop
justification: Single-author site of journalist Lucy Komisar with 141 NYC reviews from 2007 to 2026 and sustained presence in both periods. Long-running and picked up by aggregators, so keep T3.

name: BroadwayWorld
justification: BroadwayWorld, the largest theatre news site with staff and contributor reviewers in both markets and the highest volume in the corpus (503). Kept at T2 in both markets.

name: Associated Press
justification: Associated Press, the national wire service whose Broadway reviews are syndicated across US papers; long-running presence (222 NYC reviews). Kept at nyc1; London tier unchanged as it does not review there.

name: New York Theatre Guide
justification: New York Theatre Guide, an established theatre-specialist site with a roster of regular critics and strong 2022+ volume. Matches T2.

name: 1 Minute Critic
justification: 1 Minute Critic, a short-form review outlet with high 2025-2026 volume covering Broadway and Off-Broadway. Keep T3.

name: Bloomberg
justification: Bloomberg News ran regular theatre criticism (Jeremy Gerard, John Simon) until 2018; inactive since. Defunct as a theatre source; keeps the T2 tier from when it published.

name: The Daily Beast
justification: The Daily Beast, a national news site with a regular theatre critic (Tim Teeman) and sustained volume (253). Kept at T2.

name: NJ Newsroom
justification: NJ Newsroom was a New Jersey news site with a regular theatre reviewer (62 NYC reviews, 2009-2015); theatre coverage is defunct. Keep T3.

name: Pages on Stages
justification: Pages on Stages, a regular NYC theatre-specialist site with 129 reviews since 2021. Matches T3.

name: Towleroad
justification: LGBTQ news blog that ran a regular theatre column from 2015 to 2019 (62 NYC reviews), now inactive. Keep the tier it held.

name: Observer
justification: In NYC this is the New York Observer (observer.com), a recognized arts outlet that fits T2. The London rows reflect The Observer (UK Sunday paper), which the tier guide places in T2 alongside the Independent and Daily Mail, so lon1 overstates it relative to the daily nationals that set the London verdict. Considered a London move to T2 (The Observer changed ownership in 2025 and its long-time critic retired), not proposed for lack of sourced evidence. Note: this id appears to hold both the New York Observer (NYC rows) and the UK Observer (London rows).

name: Stage Left
justification: Stage Left, a NYC theatre review site active 2017-2019 (defunct in the corpus) with solid volume while active. Keep T3.

name: The New York Sun
justification: The New York Sun (relaunched online) has a regular NYC theatre critic with 118 reviews since 2022 and a solid per-year share. Keep T2.

name: Front Mezz Junkies
justification: Front Mezz Junkies is a single-editor NYC theatre site with aggregator pickup and 119 reviews since 2015. Keep T3.

name: HuffPost
justification: HuffPost carried NYC theatre reviews by known critics through its contributor platform (145 reviews, heavy in 2015-2019); theatre coverage has essentially stopped since 2022. Keep T2 as the tier that reflected its standing when it published.

name: Queerty
justification: Queerty, an LGBTQ news site with regular theatre reviews 2022-2024. Keep T3.

name: The Stage
justification: UK theatre trade paper of record with staff critics; 196 London reviews and 91 NYC reviews. Market-setting in London (T1), established trade outlet in NYC (T2); keep the split.

name: Act Three: The Reviews
justification: Single-author Blogspot theatre blog (Doug Marino) active 2016-2017, now inactive. Kept at current tier.

name: Cititour
justification: Cititour, a New York arts site whose reviews are written by veteran critic Brian Scott Lipton, with sustained volume since 2014 (292). Kept at T2.

name: The Reviews Hub
justification: Keep T2. The Reviews Hub (formerly Public Reviews, rebranded 2015) lists about 150 reviewers and 10 editors across UK regions plus New York, describing them as experienced journalists, theatre professionals and arts graduates. A T3 move was considered on the belief that reviewers are volunteers, but the site does not say so, so the move is not proposed.

name: All That Dazzles (UK)
justification: UK theatre review site with heavy, sustained London volume since 2021 (141 London reviews). Semi-pro specialist site; kept at T3.

name: As Her World Turns
justification: Personal theatre blog active 2015-2016, now inactive. Kept at current tier.

name: The Village Voice
justification: Historic NYC alternative weekly with established critics; 113 reviews, mostly before its 2018 print closure, little since. Effectively defunct for theatre; keep the T2 it held.

name: Theatre's Leiter Side
justification: Single-author blog of theatre historian Samuel L. Leiter; 56 NYC reviews, mostly 2015 to 2019, last in 2022. Recognized critic, so keep T3.

name: Bob's Theater Blog
justification: Single-author theatre blog active 2015-2017, now inactive. Kept at current tier.

name: Wolf Entertainment Guide
justification: Small entertainment review site with 37 NYC reviews from 2015 to 2019, inactive since. Keep.

name: The Telegraph
justification: The Telegraph, a UK national daily whose critics set the London verdict; its NYC reviews are a secondary market. Keep nyc2/lon1.

name: Broadway Blog
justification: Keep T2. The Broadway Blog is a NYC theatre site associated with Matthew Wexler. A T3 move was considered (it may be inactive; the site returned 503 and no 2026 posts were found) but its editorial model could not be verified, and defunct outlets keep the tier they held while publishing.

name: Los Angeles Times
justification: The Los Angeles Times is a major national paper whose chief theatre critic (Charles McNulty) reviews notable NYC productions; 84 NYC reviews. Keep T1; it does not review London shows.

name: LouReviews
justification: LouReviews appears to be a single-author London review blog with 60 reviews since 2025 and a sizeable recent share. Keep T3.

name: The New Yorker
justification: The New Yorker is a market-setting NYC publication with staff critics (Vinson Cunningham, Helen Shaw); 116 NYC reviews. Keep NYC T1; it does not review London shows.

name: Scribicide
justification: Scribicide, a small theatre review site active 2015-2019 (defunct in the corpus). Keep current T3.

name: Reviewing The Drama
justification: Small theatre review site active 2015-2017 (defunct in the corpus). Keep current T3.

name: Financial Times
justification: The Financial Times is a major international paper; in London its staff critics (Sarah Hemming and others) are among the critics who set the market, while its NYC coverage is a respected but secondary voice. The existing NYC T2 / London T1 split reflects that and it reviews in both markets.

name: Faster Times
justification: Defunct online magazine (2010-2011) with only 5 NYC reviews; a small multi-contributor site. Keep T3 as it stood when publishing.

name: Gotham Playgoer
justification: Gotham Playgoer was a single-author Blogspot theatre blog with 32 NYC reviews (2015-2019) that appeared in aggregator coverage at the time; now inactive. Keep T3.

name: Everything Theatre
justification: Everything Theatre describes itself as a 100% volunteer-run collective (founded 2011 as a two-person blog, now 60+ volunteers with volunteer editors), mostly covering London fringe and Off-West End. That editorial model fits T3, not the professional T2 outlets; propose London 2 to 3.

name: Digital Journal
justification: Digital Journal, a contributor-driven news site whose theatre coverage is incidental (27 reviews). Kept at T4.

name: Staged Theatre
justification: Unable to confirm the editorial model of stagedtheatre.co.uk, a London review site active since June 2026. Keep current T4.

name: Theatre Reviews Limited
justification: Long-running NYC theatre review site with 120 reviews from 2015 to 2026, steady presence. Semi-pro specialist site, keep T3.

name: Culture Sauce
justification: Culture Sauce, a small site run by veteran critic Thom Geier (formerly Entertainment Weekly), with strong recent volume (170 reviews). Kept at T3.

name: London Box Office
justification: London Box Office is a ticket seller that also publishes reviews and appears as an aggregator source in this project's pipeline, so some rows may be misattributed aggregator data rather than its own criticism. Flagged for review; keep current T2.

name: Melinda's Malarky
justification: Single-author Blogspot blog with 11 NYC reviews (2018-2019), likely aggregator pickup at the time; inactive. Keep T3.

name: Exeunt Magazine
justification: Exeunt NYC is a multi-contributor critical theatre magazine with an editor and longform reviews of Broadway and Off-Broadway, active for a decade with steady volume. Its standing as a recognized specialist outlet fits T2.

name: Theatre Weekly
justification: Keep T2. Theatre Weekly is an active UK theatre news and review site with named bylines and a reviewer recruitment programme. A T3 move was considered on the belief that contributors are mostly volunteers, but that could not be verified (its about page returns 404), so no move is proposed.

name: West End Best Friend
justification: London theatre blog with 83 reviews since 2023 and steady presence. Keep T3.

name: Off Script with Dan Dwyer
justification: Small personal review site active only 2018-2019 (defunct). Keep current T3; too little evidence for a move.

name: The Times (UK)
justification: UK national daily with staff critics; 158 London reviews and 24 NYC reviews. Market-setting in London, established but secondary on Broadway; keep the split.

name: Theatre Bee
justification: Small UK theatre review site with 5 London reviews in mid 2022 only. Keep.

name: London Theatre
justification: LondonTheatre.co.uk is a long-running London theatre news and reviews site with a roster of named critics, 166 London reviews concentrated since 2022. Keep T2.

name: Theatre and Tonic
justification: London theatre review site active since late 2024 with 67 London reviews. Small specialist site, keep T3.

name: Bsonarts
justification: Personal arts blog active 2017-2018, now inactive. Kept at current tier.

name: The Philadelphia Inquirer
justification: The Philadelphia Inquirer, a major metropolitan daily whose critics occasionally review Broadway. Keep T2.

name: The Spy in the Stalls
justification: Small London theatre blog that started in 2026 (23 reviews). Keep T4.

name: BackStage Barbie
justification: Single-author Blogspot theatre blog active 2015-2017, now inactive. Kept at current tier.

name: StageZine
justification: StageZine, a NY/NJ theatre site with notable 2015-2019 volume but almost none since 2022. Keep current T4; no clear evidence of higher standing.

name: A Youngish Perspective
justification: UK theatre review blog active since 2025 with steady London volume (38 reviews). Smaller semi-pro outlet; kept at T3.

name: WhatsOnStage
justification: Established UK theatre-specialist site with professional critics; 162 London reviews. Standard T2 per the rubric.

name: North West End
justification: Regional UK theatre review site with a team of volunteer reviewers covering the North West and some London shows. Recent entrant (2026) with modest volume; the current T3 fits.

name: Liam O'Dell
justification: Liam O'Dell is a freelance journalist whose own site carries 34 London reviews since 2025; single-author but a working journalist rather than a hobby blogger. Keep T3.

name: CurtainUp (defunct)
justification: CurtainUp, a long-running online theatre magazine with a stable of critics, defunct since 2020 after 129 reviews. Keeps the T2 tier from when it published.

name: Stage and Cinema
justification: Stage and Cinema, a multi-contributor theatre site with an editor and rising 2022+ volume. Keep T3.

name: Daily Mail
justification: Daily Mail, a national UK tabloid with a staff critic (Patrick Marmion) and sustained London volume (143 reviews). The tier brief lists the Daily Mail among T2 London outlets, below the Guardian, Times and Telegraph, so lon1 is out of line. Considered a London move to T2 (mass-market tabloid next to the broadsheets at T1), not proposed: the evidence was the audit rubric, not the outlet. Owner call.

name: Theater Pizzazz
justification: TheaterPizzazz.com is a NYC theatre site founded 2012, run by an editor/publisher with about 18 contributing writers, including established critics such as Carol Rocamora and Samuel L. Leiter, and a named chief theatre critic (Ron Fassler, 2026). With 177 NYC reviews that is a multi-contributor site with an editor, so T3 fits better than the T4 blog floor.

name: La Voce di New York
justification: La Voce di New York is an Italian-language New York news site with editorial staff, 27 NYC reviews since 2025. Keep T3.

name: readaboutstuff
justification: readaboutstuff.com appears to be a small London review site with 33 reviews since December 2025; its editorial model is unclear. Keep current tier.

name: The Recs
justification: Small recommendations and review site (therecs.co.uk) with 40 reviews since mid 2025, mostly on NYC shows. I cannot confirm its editorial model, so keep the current tier.

name: Theater News Online
justification: NYC theatre news and review site, 34 reviews from 2014 to 2020, now inactive (likely defunct). Keep the tier it held.

name: NorthJersey.com
justification: Website of The Record and other North Jersey daily papers, whose staff theatre critics (for example Robert Feldberg) reviewed Broadway for decades. Coverage has faded since 2022, but its standing as an established daily supports keeping T2.

name: DC Theater Arts
justification: DC Theater Arts (dctheaterarts.org) is the renamed DC Metro Theater Arts, founded 2012 and run as the nonprofit Metro Theater Arts with an editor-in-chief. Its old id dc-metro-theater-arts is T3, so propose 4 to 3 so the two ids match.

name: Evening Standard
justification: Evening Standard, a London daily whose critics set the West End verdict; NYC coverage is negligible. Keep nyc2/lon1.

name: Show Showdown
justification: Show Showdown, a personal theatre blog active 2015-2019. Keep current T3.

name: Plays International
justification: Plays International, a long-running UK theatre magazine with regular London coverage since late 2023 in the corpus. Matches T3.

name: Stage Buddy
justification: StageBuddy, a NYC theatre-specialist site with multiple contributors and sustained volume since 2015. Keep T3.

name: London Unattached
justification: London Unattached is a London lifestyle blog with occasional theatre reviews (34 since 2025) and no recognized-critic status. Keep T4.

name: Parade
justification: Parade magazine, a national Sunday supplement; theatre reviews are incidental (5 in 2018). Kept at T2 per the default-keep rule, though it is a candidate for review if more data appears.

name: Broadway & Me
justification: Broadway & Me, a single-author blog by Jan Simpson with sustained volume since 2015 (44 reviews). Kept at current tier.

name: This Week in New York
justification: NYC events newsletter (twi-ny.com) with largely single-author coverage; 57 reviews. Keep T4.

name: Lighting & Sound America
justification: Lighting & Sound America is a professional theatre-technology trade magazine whose editors review NYC productions with design focus; 218 NYC reviews since 2015 with steady presence. Keep T2.

name: The Upcoming
justification: London culture webzine with many unpaid contributors; 35 London reviews since 2025. Keep T4.

name: Stu on Broadway
justification: Stu on Broadway, a single-author Broadway blog active 2011-2018 (defunct in the corpus). Keep current T3.

name: The Independent
justification: The Independent is a UK national with established theatre critics, a regular London voice (72 London reviews) and an occasional NYC reviewer (13). Keep NYC T2 / London T1.

name: Simon Seez
justification: Simon Seez, Simon Saltzman's blog; Saltzman is a long-time New Jersey theatre critic. Low volume 2016-2017; keep T3.

name: Musical Theatre Review
justification: Musical Theatre Review is an established UK specialist site with named critics, 66 reviews across both markets (2015-2021) and inactive since. Keep T3 as it stood when publishing.

name: Carey Purcell
justification: Freelance theatre writer Carey Purcell with 6 reviews in 2016-2017 and no outlet domain recorded. Unclear what outlet carried these; kept at current tier.

name: Zeal NYC
justification: NYC lifestyle and culture site with 44 reviews from 2014 to 2018, inactive since. Keep the tier it held.

name: Center On The Aisle
justification: Small theatre review site active 2015-2018, now inactive. Kept at current tier.

name: City Cabaret
justification: Cabaret and theatre review site active 2016-2019, now inactive. Kept at current tier.

name: Reflections in the Light
justification: Reflections in the Light, Lauren Yarger's Christian-perspective theatre blog, active in the corpus 2014-2018. Keep T3.

name: NJ.com
justification: NJ.com carries the Star-Ledger's theatre criticism, a long-standing professional daily critic with 82 NYC reviews (mostly before 2020). Keep T2.

name: Chelsea Community News
justification: Hyperlocal Manhattan community news site with incidental theatre coverage (10 reviews). Kept at T4.

name: NewNowNext
justification: NewNowNext was Logo TV's LGBTQ entertainment site with occasional theatre reviews (10, 2017-2019); defunct. Keep T3.

name: Time Out London
justification: Time Out London is an established listings and culture magazine with staff critics and 174 London reviews, but the rubric's London T1 is the major national papers plus The Stage, and it lists Time Out at T2. NYC tier unchanged. Considered London T1 to T2, not proposed: Time Out London is a leading London theatre voice with an established chief critic, so T1 stands.

name: Monstagigz
justification: Monstagigz appears to be a small UK music and theatre review blog with 24 London reviews since late 2025. Keep T3; not enough information to justify a move.

name: London Pub Theatres
justification: London Pub Theatres is a fringe-focused London magazine site with 15 reviews since 2026. Keep T3.

name: Out Magazine
justification: Out, a national LGBTQ magazine with occasional theatre reviews; no theatre reviews in the corpus since 2019. Keep T3.

name: The Epoch Times
justification: The Epoch Times, a national newspaper with regular theatre reviews in 2015-2017 (19). Kept at T3.

name: The Jewish Chronicle
justification: Long-running UK national Jewish weekly with a regular theatre critic; 24 London reviews since 2025. A niche-audience paper with a real critic fits T3.

name: LondonTheatre1
justification: LondonTheatre1 is a long-running multi-reviewer London theatre site with 125 London reviews, mostly since 2022. Keep T2.

name: British Theatre Guide
justification: Keep T2 for now, but this id needs splitting before any tier call: 48 of its 98 rows link to British Theatre Guide (britishtheatreguide.info, a long-running UK review site with established critics), 9 to BritishTheatre.com (a smaller news and review site) and 41 have no URL. A T3 demotion was considered for BritishTheatre.com but would also hit the British Theatre Guide rows.

name: On Off Broadway
justification: Small site with 15 reviews all dated to a single day in 2010, likely a bulk import or index page rather than a sustained outlet. Keep current T3.

name: Times Square Chronicles
justification: NYC theatre and nightlife site (t2conline.com) with 62 reviews and a promotional slant. Keep T4.

name: The Arts Desk
justification: The Arts Desk, a UK arts site staffed by former national-newspaper critics, with steady London volume (120 reviews). Matches the T2 anchor list.

name: Theatrecat
justification: Blog of Libby Purves, former chief theatre critic of The Times; 32 London reviews since 2023. Single-author, but a recognized critic, so T3 rather than T4.

name: Journal Inquirer
justification: The Journal Inquirer is a small Connecticut daily newspaper; 5 NYC reviews in 2018. Keep T3 as a local paper.

name: Labor Press
justification: LaborPress is a New York labor-news site with occasional theatre reviews (12, 2016-2018), now inactive for theatre. Keep T3.

name: The i
justification: The i is a UK national daily whose theatre critics are regulars in London review coverage (46 London reviews, rising since 2022). The existing London T1 / NYC T2 split stands; it does not review NYC shows.

name: Fordham Observer
justification: Fordham University's Lincoln Center student newspaper, 8 NYC reviews in 2017-2018, now inactive. A student paper is at the low end of T3 but with aggregator-era pickup it stays at T3.

name: Drama Queen NYC
justification: Small New York theatre blog active 2015-2019, now inactive. Kept at current tier.

name: Broadway Showbiz
justification: Small theatre blog active 2015-2017, now inactive. Kept at current tier.

name: The Contending
justification: The Contending appears to be a small culture site with 20 NYC reviews since late 2024; editorial model unclear. Keep current T3.

name: First Night Magazine
justification: A newer London theatre magazine site with 23 reviews since December 2025; a small specialist outlet. Keep T3.

name: Onandoffbroadwaytheaterreviews
justification: Small theatre review blog active 2018-2019, now apparently inactive. Keep current T3.

name: 2ontheaisle
justification: Small WordPress theatre blog that covered Broadway in 2015-2017 and is now inactive. Kept at current tier as no evidence it ranks lower or higher.

name: New York Classical Review
justification: New York Classical Review is a professional music criticism site with established critics, reviewing opera and music theatre in NYC (21 since 2024). Keep T3.

name: Off Off Online
justification: OffOffOnline is a long-running multi-contributor site focused on Off-Off-Broadway, with growing 2022+ volume. It could argue for T3, but its scope is fringe-focused and the current T4 is defensible; keep.

name: The Cultural Critic
justification: The Cultural Critic, a small review site active 2016-2017 (defunct in the corpus). Keep current T3.

name: The Clyde Fitch Report
justification: The Clyde Fitch Report, an arts and politics site with an editor and multiple contributors, active 2015-2017 in the corpus. Keep T3.

name: Simon Parris Man In Chair
justification: Simon Parris: Man in Chair, an Australian single-author theatre blog with occasional NYC reviews 2015-2018. Keep current T3.

name: Diandra Reviews It All
justification: Personal review blog active 2017-2018, now inactive. Kept at current tier.

name: Magical Misstari Tour
justification: Single-author Blogspot blog with 7 NYC reviews (2016-2018), likely aggregator pickup at the time; inactive. Keep T3.

name: Adventuresintheatreland
justification: UK theatre blog that began reviewing London shows in August 2026 (11 reviews). Too new to judge a move; kept at current tier.

name: Showbiz411
justification: Showbiz411, Roger Friedman's entertainment news site with occasional theatre reviews, little activity since 2019. Keep current T3.

name: WNYC
justification: New York public radio station with a regular theatre critic; 34 NYC reviews from 2016 to 2019, theatre reviews inactive since. Keep the T2 it held.

name: Flipsidereviews
justification: Single-author Blogspot blog with 5 NYC reviews in 2015-2016, likely picked up via an aggregator (Show Score) at the time; inactive since. Low volume alone does not justify a move, keep T3.

name: Theater In The Now
justification: Small NYC theatre site with 6 reviews, all from late 2015, apparently defunct. Keep the tier it held.

name: Afridiziak Theatre News
justification: Long-running London site covering Black British theatre, with regular London reviews since 2024 (26). Niche specialist outlet; kept at current tier.

name: Broadway Journal
justification: Small theatre review site active 2018-2019, now inactive. Kept at current tier.

name: Bachtrack
justification: Bachtrack, an international classical music, opera and dance review site with occasional theatre reviews in both markets (11). Kept at T3.

name: Fringereview
justification: FringeReview is a UK multi-reviewer site covering fringe and London theatre, active with 18 London reviews since 2025. Keep T3.

name: Londonlivinglarge
justification: London Living Large appears to be a London lifestyle blog with 10 theatre reviews since August 2026. Keep T3; not enough information to justify a move.

name: City A.M.
justification: City A.M., a free London business daily with a regular theatre critic, steady since 2023 (29 London reviews). Kept at T3.

name: Radio Times
justification: Radio Times, a national UK listings magazine whose theatre reviews are occasional but carry editorial oversight. Keep T3.

name: South London
justification: southlondon.co.uk is a local news site from Community Matters Media Ltd (publisher of Southwark News and South London Weekly) that runs bylined theatre reviews. It is not the South London Press, which closed in 2025. A local news publisher with editorial oversight fits T3 rather than the T4 blog floor.

name: Aleks Sierz
justification: Personal site of Aleks Sierz, a recognized UK critic and author (Theatre Record, The Arts Desk). Keep T3.

name: Theartsdispatch
justification: Substack newsletter with 9 reviews since 2026, mostly London. Likely single-author, but I cannot confirm who writes it, so keep the current tier.

name: Upstage Downstage
justification: Blogspot theatre blog with 7 NYC reviews from 2016 to 2019, inactive. Keep.

name: Film Festival Traveler
justification: Small film-focused site whose theatre coverage was occasional (11 NYC reviews, 2015-2017, now inactive). Keep T3.

name: Slant Magazine
justification: Slant Magazine, an established film and culture magazine with an editor and regular theatre reviews since 2016. Keep T2.
